record.paper_title: Open problems in local discrete holomorphic dynamics
record.original_question: For a non-invertible dominant germ f in End(C^n, O), does the sequence of orders of its iterates, {c(f^k)}_{k∈N}, eventually satisfy a linear recurrence relation with integer coefficients?

evidence.quote: (OP6) Let f ∈ End(C^n, O) be non-invertible and dominant. Is it true that the sequence {c(f^k)}k∈N satisfies, at least for k large enough, a linear recursion formula with integer coefficients?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,O)\to(\mathbb{C}^n,O)$ be a holomorphic germ fixing the origin, written componentwise as $f=(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ with each $f_j\in\mathbb{C}\{z_1,\dots,z_n\}$ vanishing at $O$. Define the order of $f$ at $O$ by
$$c(f)=\min_{1\le j\le n}\operatorname{ord}_O(f_j),$$
where $\operatorname{ord}_O(g)$ is the smallest total degree of a nonzero monomial appearing in the Taylor expansion of $g$ at $O$. Assume that $f$ is dominant (the Jacobian determinant of $f$ does not vanish identically) and non-invertible (so $df_O$ is not invertible, equivalently $c(f)\ge 1$ and $f$ is not a biholomorphism). Let $f^k$ denote the $k$-fold composition of $f$ with itself.

Question: Does the sequence $\{c(f^k)\}_{k\in\mathbb{N}}$ satisfy, for all sufficiently large $k$, a linear recurrence relation
$$c(f^{k+r})=a_{r-1}\,c(f^{k+r-1})+\cdots+a_1\,c(f^{k+1})+a_0\,c(f^k)$$
with coefficients $a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{r-1}\in\mathbb{Z}$?
artifact.status_search_result: In dimension $n=2$, for dominant superattracting holomorphic germs $f:(\mathbb{C}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^2,0)$, Gignac (arXiv:1209.3450, 2012) proved that $\{c(f^k)\}$ eventually satisfies an integral linear recursion of order at most two (after possibly replacing $f$ by an iterate), using valuative techniques. The general case in arbitrary dimension $n\ge 2$ for all non-invertible dominant germs does not appear to be established in the literature, so the problem remains open in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Growth of attraction rates for iterates of a superattracting germ in dimension two
status_evidence.snippet: this sequence eventually satisfies an integral linear recursion relation, which, up to replacing f by an iterate, can be taken to have order at most two
status_evidence.claim: The recursion property is established for dominant superattracting germs in dimension 2.
